source_caption:
The classroom scene in The Social Network is so memorable because Mark barely reacts when the professor tries to embarrass him in front of everyone. Instead of arguing, he fires back the correct answer while walking out — a perfect early glimpse of the character’s mix of arrogance, intelligence, and total indifference to authority. That tiny exchange tells you almost everything about him before the real story even begins.

The Social Network (2010), directed by David Fincher, starring Jesse Eisenberg, Andrew Garfield, Justin Timberlake. A razor-sharp and propulsive drama that captures the birth of Facebook, exposing ambition, betrayal, and genius in one of the defining stories of the digital age.

source_details.title: The Social Network
source_details.synopsis: The Social Network is a 2010 American biographical drama film directed by David Fincher and written by Aaron Sorkin. Based on the 2009 book The Accidental Billionaires by Ben Mezrich, the film portrays the founding of the social networking website Facebook. It stars Jesse Eisenberg as Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg, with Andrew Garfield as co-founder Eduardo Saverin, Justin Timberlake as Sean Parker, Armie Hammer as Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss, and Max Minghella as Divya Narendra. Neither Zuckerberg nor any other Facebook staff were involved with the project, although Saverin was a consultant for Mezrich's book. Production began when Sorkin signed on to write the screenplay.
